market_holds: Q3 (Oct qtr) is effectively pre-announced: on 2026-10-15 (8-K item 7.01) Semtech raised Q3 to net sales $417.5M +/- $2.5M (from $410M +/- $5M), adj GM 59.0%, adj op margin 33.0% +/- 10bp, adj EPS $1.14 +/- $0.02, about 10 days before the quarter closed. Consensus seen at $1.13 to $1.15 EPS and $416M to $424M revenue (Earnings Whispers/finviz preview 2026-11-15; Chartmill), so it sits on the raised guide. Q4 consensus is uncertain, roughly $437M to $450M on Benzinga pages (snippet only, undated), and it probably still includes the cellular module business being sold to Compal, with closing expected in fiscal Q4. Options (baseline sealed 18:08 UTC today): front-week straddle 13.5%, event-implied about 5.3% after taking out 146% annualised realised vol, 25-delta skew +16.7 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.21. Run-in: -24% over 20 days, -48% from the 2026-10-06 high of $197, about in line with CRDO -45%, MRVL -50% and ALAB -44% over the same span, while SOXX fell 29%. The two moves that were the company's own were -10% on the analyst day where it raised (2026-10-15) and a Susquehanna target cut from $200 to $170 on 2026-11-20 (rating kept positive). Today it is +17% intraday with SOXX +13% and the Nasdaq about +6% on Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang, after the Nasdaq 100's worst week since 2020. On the last eight prints the next open gapped +18.8, +13.9, -1.7, +7.0, -1.9, -6.5, +4.8 and +2.7%.
view: Semtech's Q3 is known. Management tightened it to a $5M range ten days before quarter end and consensus moved onto it, so the reaction turns on the Q4 guide (data center growth on the 1.6T FiberEdge, ACC and LPO ramp, and how the cellular divestiture is shown) and on FY28 supply. The inputs mostly point the right way. Management guided well above consensus in May (Q2 $328M vs $299.5M) and August (Q3 $410M vs $357M), then raised again mid-quarter. In August it said the rest of FY27 was booked, more than 70% of the FY28 target was covered, and year-over-year growth would accelerate into Q4. Counterparties since then are strong: Nvidia guided its next quarter to $130B against $125B expected (reported 2026-11-17); Innolight said 1.6T revenue growth accelerated in Q3; MACOM guided data center +15% q/q for the Dec quarter and an 80% FY27 base case (2026-11-05). Against that: (1) the bar has caught up. The FY30 framework ($3.2B sales, $2.1B data center, $12.40 to $13.00 EPS) is public and Q4 consensus already implies about 57-60% y/y. (2) Supply binds. Management warned secured capacity may not cover 2H FY28, AAOI says 1.6T DSPs are short until about 1Q27, and the Tower SiGe expansion is not producing yet. (3) The headline Q4 revenue guide can land below a consensus that still carries cellular revenue if the Compal sale closes early in the quarter, even though management says the sale is EPS-neutral. (4) A raise has already been sold once: -10% on the analyst day. (5) In this tape the overnight move is dominated by the market. SOXX gapped between -6.7% and +15.2% at the open on many days this month, and optical peers gapped 5-9%. My read is a modest lean up: the company's own cadence and its counterparties support a like-for-like Q4 guide at or above consensus. The price fell with the group, not on company news, so the release can be judged on its own numbers. But consensus already reflects the analyst-day framework and the divestiture optics are a coin flip, so I cannot show a gap the price has missed.

recommendation.reason: The Q3 numbers were pre-announced on 2026-10-15 and consensus sits on them, so the print turns on the Q4 guide and the FY28 supply commentary. Company cadence and counterparties (Nvidia, Innolight, MACOM) favour a like-for-like beat, but consensus already reflects the FY30 framework. Supply limits, the way the divestiture is presented and an overnight tape swinging 5-15% a day leave the direction near a coin flip, well short of 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 data center guide implying sequential growth of 25% or more on a like-for-like basis, with capacity commentary that lifts the FY28 supply ceiling, would make me a buyer at the open. A headline Q4 revenue guide below about $430M without a clean ex-cellular bridge would point down.

self_critique: The strongest case for a bigger lean up: every recent guide has landed well above consensus (May +9.5%, Aug +15%), management said Q4 is booked and y/y accelerates, and the stock trades about 48% below its high on sector fear rather than company data. A clean beat-and-raise in a market that just turned up could gap it +10-15%, and I may be under-weighting that because the bar looks met. The strongest case for down: consensus already carries the FY30 framework; supply is the binding constraint, so Q4 upside is capped; the divestiture can make the headline guide look sequentially flat; puts carry a 17-point skew premium; and a +17% relief day into the print leaves room for give-back overnight. These roughly cancel, which is why I stay near 50 and do not recommend.
approach_notes: P6's split of the run-in into tape and company news was decisive here: it showed the drawdown is sector-driven. P4's 'priced is a claim to prove' helped identify that the Q3 bar had been moved by the company's own 8-K. P7's push to estimate the invisible line was hard to apply where the deciding guide is muddled by a mid-quarter divestiture and an overnight tape whose noise exceeds the event move.
